headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty snapped two-week gains as surging crude oil prices dragged equities lower.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 26 October.

why: Surging crude oil prices hitting six-month highs dragged Indian shares to weekly losses.
Sensex and Nifty snapped their two-week winning streak, falling around 2% over the week.
Geopolitical tension and rising oil prices to $117/bbl increased market volatility.
Heavy selling pressure across major sectors pulled benchmark indices down despite intermittent rebounds in IT stocks.
whatHappening: Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a 26% YoY rise in Q2 consolidated net profit to ₹5,645 crore with NII up 16%.
FDA issued a recall order for a batch of Patanjali Foods' Cow Ghee in Madhya Pradesh.
SEBI announced plans to review short selling and SLB rules while developing an AI sandbox and bond market-making framework.
Adani Enterprises emerged as the top loser in the market weekly wrap.
summary: In the last trading session, Indian equities snapped their two-week winning streak as surging crude oil prices weighed heavily on market sentiment. On the corporate front, Kotak Mahindra Bank delivered strong Q2 profit growth, while Patanjali Foods faced regulatory heat over a product recall. Markets remain closed today for the weekend and will resume trading on Monday, 26 October.
